study.title: Use of high-speed angiography (HSA)-derived boundary conditions and physics informed neural networks (PINNs) for comprehensive estimation of neurovascular hemodynamics
study.venue: Proceedings of SPIE (Medical Imaging 2023: Physics of Medical Imaging, Vol. 12463)

imaging.modality_detail: 1000 fps high-speed angiography (HSA) in vitro in 3D-printed phantoms, plus CFD-simulated (in silico, passive scalar) 1000 fps angiograms
imaging.territory_detail: Carotid artery bifurcation phantom, basilar tip saccular aneurysm (in silico), simple carotid artery bend (in silico)
imaging.frames_per_sequence: 1500 frames (in vitro carotid bifurcation); 650 frames for the next longest acquisition

task.task_description: Physics-informed neural network constrained by Navier-Stokes, convection and conservation equations plus HSA-derived contrast boundary conditions to estimate velocity, pressure and contrast fields over (x, y, t) from angiographic sequences.
task.clinical_application: Patient-specific neurovascular hemodynamics (velocimetry and pressure) for aneurysms and carotid vessels without assumed inlet boundary conditions

architecture_names: fully connected DNN (10 hidden layers x 250 nodes)

temporal_evidence.quote: A PINN based on an objective function comprised of the NavierStokes equation, the convection equation, and angiography-based BCs was used for estimation of velocity, pressure and contrast flow at every point in the lattice.

metrics.metric: average minimum convergence time (incl. pre-processing and PINN training)
minimum convergence time (less consistent convergence, 350 epochs)

G3.quote: Calculations were performed on a 3D lattice comprised of 2D projections temporally stacked over the angiographic sequence.

G5.quote: This means that no ground truth labels are required

other_limitations: PINN must be retrained for each input acquisition
Pressure is unconstrained; velocities distal to the contrast leading edge are underapproximated and pressure was erroneous in the healthy carotid model
Velocity predictions restricted to contrast-filled regions
Minimum collocation points and convergence criteria not rigorously assessed
Quantum mottle in in vitro HSA increases training time
future_work: Use contrast dilution gradient (CDG) velocity estimates as initial condition to speed PINN training
Replace fixed epoch limit with an error tolerance threshold as convergence criterion
